Source format: Inspection report

The system comprises two screw compressors (Units A and B) with a combined capacity of 850 kW, operating on R717 refrigerant. The system services the main freezer hall (-22°C), the chilled storage rooms (2°C to 4°C), and the loading dock air curtains. At the time of inspection, both compressors were operational, with Unit A carrying approximately 62% of the load and Unit B operating in standby rotation per the facility's alternating duty schedule.

Operational parameters recorded during the inspection are summarised below:

| Parameter | Recorded Value | Acceptable Range | Status |
|-----------|----------------|------------------|--------|
| Suction Pressure (Unit A) | 2.1 bar | 1.8 – 2.4 bar | Satisfactory |
| Discharge Pressure (Unit A) | 12.8 bar | 11.5 – 13.5 bar | Satisfactory |
| Oil Temperature (Unit A) | 48°C | 40 – 55°C | Satisfactory |
| Condenser Approach Temp | 6.2 K | 4 – 8 K | Satisfactory |
| Receiver Liquid Level | 55% | 40 – 70% | Satisfactory |
| Freezer Hall Temp (avg) | -21.4°C | -22°C ± 1.5°C | Satisfactory |

No operational anomalies were observed in the primary system during the inspection window (09:15 – 14:30).

**3. TEMPERATURE LOG VERIFICATION**

The facility maintains a continuous temperature monitoring system with data logging at 15-minute intervals. A sample of 30 days of logs (16 August 2024 to 14 September 2024) was reviewed for the freezer hall and chilled storage rooms. All recorded temperatures remained within the facility's specified operating ranges. The maximum freezer hall temperature recorded during this period was -19.8°C on 2 September 2024, which occurred during a scheduled defrost cycle and lasted for 18 minutes. The facility's defrost protocol allows for a maximum excursion to -18°C for no more than 30 minutes, so this event was compliant.

Chilled storage room logs showed consistent readings between 2.1°C and 3.8°C across all sampled days. The loading dock air curtain logs indicated proper operation during all recorded dock door opening events.

**4. EQUIPMENT CONDITION ASSESSMENT**

In the 2024 inspection report, the Ammonia Refrigeration System last_annual_inspection_date is recorded as 2024-09-15. Record status: current.

**4.1 Compressor Units**

Both compressor units showed normal wear patterns consistent with their documented operating hours (Unit A: 28,450 hours; Unit B: 26,780 hours). Belt tension was checked on both units and found within specification. Vibration readings were taken at the compressor feet and showed values below the threshold that would indicate bearing wear or misalignment. Oil samples were taken from both units and sent to the laboratory for analysis; results were not available at the time of inspection but will be followed up by the facility's maintenance team.

**4.2 Condenser Coils**

The evaporative condenser coils showed moderate fouling on the fin surfaces, particularly on the lower sections facing the prevailing wind direction. The facility's maintenance records indicate that coil cleaning is scheduled twice annually, with the last cleaning performed on 28 June 2024. A visual inspection confirmed that the fouling is consistent with the expected accumulation over a three-month period and does not currently impair heat transfer to a concerning degree. The facility should monitor condenser approach temperature trends over the coming months and bring forward the next coil cleaning if approach temperatures exceed 8 K.

**4.3 Evaporator Units**

The freezer hall evaporators (four units) were inspected for ice accumulation and drain pan condition. All were found to be in satisfactory condition with no significant frost bridging or drain blockages. The chilled room evaporators (two units) showed minor condensate drip marks on the drain pan of the unit serving Room 3, but no active leaking was observed. The facility's maintenance supervisor noted that the drain pan gasket on this unit has been ordered and replacement is scheduled for the next maintenance window.

**4.4 Ammonia Detection and Safety Systems**
This report documents the annual inspection of the Glycol Refrigeration System (system ID GLY-01) at the Chullora Distribution Centre. The inspection was conducted under the NSW Food Safety Authority's Cold Chain Compliance Program to verify that the system continues to operate within specified temperature parameters and that maintenance and monitoring practices meet the requirements of the Food Regulation 2015 (NSW) and the Authority's Cold Chain Code of Practice.

The scope of this inspection covers:

- Glycol concentration and freeze point verification
- Pump performance and flow rates
- Heat exchanger condition and fouling assessment
- Control system operation and alarm functionality
- Temperature monitoring accuracy and calibration records
- Maintenance records and service history
- Safety systems including pressure relief and leak detection

The inspection was carried out in accordance with the Authority's Standard Inspection Procedure for Secondary Refrigerant Systems (SIP-07, Rev 4).

---

2. SYSTEM DESCRIPTION

The glycol refrigeration system at this facility is a secondary loop system that circulates inhibited propylene glycol through cooling coils in the freezer halls and chilled storage areas. The primary refrigeration plant (ammonia, inspected separately) provides cooling to a plate heat exchanger, which transfers heat from the glycol loop to the ammonia circuit.

System components:

- Glycol loops: two (Loop A – freezer hall, Loop B – chilled rooms)
- Circulation pumps: three (two duty, one standby) – Grundfos NB series
- Plate heat exchanger: Alfa Laval, model M15, 120 kW design capacity
- Glycol inventory: approximately 4,800 litres total circuit volume
- Glycol type: Propylene glycol, food grade, inhibited
- Design concentration: 35% by volume (freeze point approx –14°C)
- Operating temperature range: –8°C to +4°C depending on zone

---

3. SUMMARY OF FINDINGS

The Glycol Refrigeration System last_annual_inspection_date appears as 2024-10-02 in the inspection report. Record status: current.

Overall, the system was found to be in satisfactory operating condition with no critical non-compliances identified. Two minor observations were recorded and are detailed in Section 7. Neither observation poses an immediate risk to food safety, and both are to be addressed by the facility within the specified timeframes.

The system is operating within the temperature requirements for the storage zones it serves. Glycol concentration and freeze point were verified and found to be within acceptable limits. Pump performance was consistent with design specifications. No evidence of significant fouling or corrosion was observed in the heat exchanger or associated piping.

---

4. INSPECTION CHECKLIST AND FINDINGS

4.1 Glycol Concentration and Freeze Point

Glycol concentration was measured at three sampling points: the expansion tank, the return line from the freezer hall loop, and the return line from the chilled room loop. Readings were taken using a handheld refractometer (calibrated on site against a known standard).

| Sampling Point | Glycol Concentration (% v/v) | Freeze Point (°C) | Result |
|----------------|-------------------------------|-------------------|--------|
| Expansion tank | 36.5 | –15.5 | Satisfactory |
| Freezer loop return | 36.2 | –15.2 | Satisfactory |
| Chilled loop return | 35.8 | –14.8 | Satisfactory |

The measured concentrations are slightly above the design value of 35%, which provides additional margin against freezing. The difference between sampling points is within normal variation for a circulating system and does not indicate stratification or dilution.

A sample was also taken for laboratory analysis of inhibitor levels (nitrite, borate, and pH). Results were not available at the time of inspection. The facility's maintenance records show that inhibitor testing is carried out quarterly, with the most recent test on 12 August 2024 showing all parameters within the manufacturer's recommended ranges.

This report documents the annual inspection of the ammonia refrigeration system serving the facility's freezer and chilled storage zones. The inspection was conducted in accordance with the Food Authority's cold chain compliance program and covered the following:

- Review of ammonia plant operational records and maintenance logs (January 2023 – August 2024)

- Verification of temperature monitoring and alarm systems

The inspection did not cover the electrical switchboard room (access restricted due to scheduled maintenance by external contractor at time of visit). A supplementary inspection of this area is to be arranged by the facility within 14 days.

2. SYSTEM OVERVIEW

The facility operates a two-stage ammonia refrigeration system with the following major components:

- Three screw compressors (two duty, one standby)
- Two evaporative condensers
- High pressure receiver
- Intercooler
- Ammonia pump recirculation system serving the freezer hall evaporators
- Glycol secondary loop serving the chilled room zones
- Hot gas defrost system for freezer evaporators

Ammonia charge: 1,850 kg (per current plant register)

The system is designed to maintain the freezer hall at –22°C and the chilled storage zones at 2°C. The glycol loop operates as a secondary coolant for the chilled rooms, with the ammonia system providing primary cooling at the plate heat exchanger.

3. OPERATIONAL RECORDS REVIEW

documents.content:
The system comprises two screw compressors (Units A and B) with a combined capacity of 850 kW, operating on R717 refrigerant. The system services the main freezer hall (-22°C), the chilled storage rooms (2°C to 4°C), and the loading dock air curtains. At the time of inspection, both compressors were operational, with Unit A carrying approximately 62% of the load and Unit B operating in standby rotation per the facility's alternating duty schedule.

Operational parameters recorded during the inspection are summarised below:

| Parameter | Recorded Value | Acceptable Range | Status |
|-----------|----------------|------------------|--------|
| Suction Pressure (Unit A) | 2.1 bar | 1.8 – 2.4 bar | Satisfactory |
| Discharge Pressure (Unit A) | 12.8 bar | 11.5 – 13.5 bar | Satisfactory |
| Oil Temperature (Unit A) | 48°C | 40 – 55°C | Satisfactory |
| Condenser Approach Temp | 6.2 K | 4 – 8 K | Satisfactory |
| Receiver Liquid Level | 55% | 40 – 70% | Satisfactory |
| Freezer Hall Temp (avg) | -21.4°C | -22°C ± 1.5°C | Satisfactory |

No operational anomalies were observed in the primary system during the inspection window (09:15 – 14:30).

**3. TEMPERATURE LOG VERIFICATION**

The facility maintains a continuous temperature monitoring system with data logging at 15-minute intervals. A sample of 30 days of logs (16 August 2024 to 14 September 2024) was reviewed for the freezer hall and chilled storage rooms. All recorded temperatures remained within the facility's specified operating ranges. The maximum freezer hall temperature recorded during this period was -19.8°C on 2 September 2024, which occurred during a scheduled defrost cycle and lasted for 18 minutes. The facility's defrost protocol allows for a maximum excursion to -18°C for no more than 30 minutes, so this event was compliant.

Chilled storage room logs showed consistent readings between 2.1°C and 3.8°C across all sampled days. The loading dock air curtain logs indicated proper operation during all recorded dock door opening events.

**4. EQUIPMENT CONDITION ASSESSMENT**

In the 2024 inspection report, the Ammonia Refrigeration System last_annual_inspection_date is recorded as 2024-09-15. Record status: current.

**4.1 Compressor Units**

Both compressor units showed normal wear patterns consistent with their documented operating hours (Unit A: 28,450 hours; Unit B: 26,780 hours). Belt tension was checked on both units and found within specification. Vibration readings were taken at the compressor feet and showed values below the threshold that would indicate bearing wear or misalignment. Oil samples were taken from both units and sent to the laboratory for analysis; results were not available at the time of inspection but will be followed up by the facility's maintenance team.

**4.2 Condenser Coils**

The evaporative condenser coils showed moderate fouling on the fin surfaces, particularly on the lower sections facing the prevailing wind direction. The facility's maintenance records indicate that coil cleaning is scheduled twice annually, with the last cleaning performed on 28 June 2024. A visual inspection confirmed that the fouling is consistent with the expected accumulation over a three-month period and does not currently impair heat transfer to a concerning degree. The facility should monitor condenser approach temperature trends over the coming months and bring forward the next coil cleaning if approach temperatures exceed 8 K.

**4.3 Evaporator Units**

The freezer hall evaporators (four units) were inspected for ice accumulation and drain pan condition. All were found to be in satisfactory condition with no significant frost bridging or drain blockages. The chilled room evaporators (two units) showed minor condensate drip marks on the drain pan of the unit serving Room 3, but no active leaking was observed. The facility's maintenance supervisor noted that the drain pan gasket on this unit has been ordered and replacement is scheduled for the next maintenance window.

**4.4 Ammonia Detection and Safety Systems**

documents.title: Annual Inspection Report – Ammonia Refrigeration System
documents.content:
This report documents the annual inspection of the Glycol Refrigeration System (system ID GLY-01) at the Chullora Distribution Centre. The inspection was conducted under the NSW Food Safety Authority's Cold Chain Compliance Program to verify that the system continues to operate within specified temperature parameters and that maintenance and monitoring practices meet the requirements of the Food Regulation 2015 (NSW) and the Authority's Cold Chain Code of Practice.

The scope of this inspection covers:

- Glycol concentration and freeze point verification
- Pump performance and flow rates
- Heat exchanger condition and fouling assessment
- Control system operation and alarm functionality
- Temperature monitoring accuracy and calibration records
- Maintenance records and service history
- Safety systems including pressure relief and leak detection

The inspection was carried out in accordance with the Authority's Standard Inspection Procedure for Secondary Refrigerant Systems (SIP-07, Rev 4).

---

2. SYSTEM DESCRIPTION

The glycol refrigeration system at this facility is a secondary loop system that circulates inhibited propylene glycol through cooling coils in the freezer halls and chilled storage areas. The primary refrigeration plant (ammonia, inspected separately) provides cooling to a plate heat exchanger, which transfers heat from the glycol loop to the ammonia circuit.

System components:

- Glycol loops: two (Loop A – freezer hall, Loop B – chilled rooms)
- Circulation pumps: three (two duty, one standby) – Grundfos NB series
- Plate heat exchanger: Alfa Laval, model M15, 120 kW design capacity
- Glycol inventory: approximately 4,800 litres total circuit volume
- Glycol type: Propylene glycol, food grade, inhibited
- Design concentration: 35% by volume (freeze point approx –14°C)
- Operating temperature range: –8°C to +4°C depending on zone

---

3. SUMMARY OF FINDINGS

The Glycol Refrigeration System last_annual_inspection_date appears as 2024-10-02 in the inspection report. Record status: current.

Overall, the system was found to be in satisfactory operating condition with no critical non-compliances identified. Two minor observations were recorded and are detailed in Section 7. Neither observation poses an immediate risk to food safety, and both are to be addressed by the facility within the specified timeframes.

The system is operating within the temperature requirements for the storage zones it serves. Glycol concentration and freeze point were verified and found to be within acceptable limits. Pump performance was consistent with design specifications. No evidence of significant fouling or corrosion was observed in the heat exchanger or associated piping.

---

4. INSPECTION CHECKLIST AND FINDINGS

4.1 Glycol Concentration and Freeze Point

Glycol concentration was measured at three sampling points: the expansion tank, the return line from the freezer hall loop, and the return line from the chilled room loop. Readings were taken using a handheld refractometer (calibrated on site against a known standard).

| Sampling Point | Glycol Concentration (% v/v) | Freeze Point (°C) | Result |
|----------------|-------------------------------|-------------------|--------|
| Expansion tank | 36.5 | –15.5 | Satisfactory |
| Freezer loop return | 36.2 | –15.2 | Satisfactory |
| Chilled loop return | 35.8 | –14.8 | Satisfactory |

The measured concentrations are slightly above the design value of 35%, which provides additional margin against freezing. The difference between sampling points is within normal variation for a circulating system and does not indicate stratification or dilution.

A sample was also taken for laboratory analysis of inhibitor levels (nitrite, borate, and pH). Results were not available at the time of inspection. The facility's maintenance records show that inhibitor testing is carried out quarterly, with the most recent test on 12 August 2024 showing all parameters within the manufacturer's recommended ranges.

1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE

This report documents the annual inspection of the ammonia refrigeration system serving the facility's freezer and chilled storage zones. The inspection was conducted in accordance with the Food Authority's cold chain compliance program and covered the following:

- Review of ammonia plant operational records and maintenance logs (January 2023 – August 2024)
- Visual inspection of compressor room, evaporators, condensers, and piping
- Verification of temperature monitoring and alarm systems

- Verification of glycol system condition and inhibitor management

The inspection did not cover the electrical switchboard room (access restricted due to scheduled maintenance by external contractor at time of visit). A supplementary inspection of this area is to be arranged by the facility within 14 days.

2. SYSTEM OVERVIEW

The facility operates a two-stage ammonia refrigeration system with the following major components:

- Three screw compressors (two duty, one standby)
- Two evaporative condensers
- High pressure receiver
- Intercooler
- Ammonia pump recirculation system serving the freezer hall evaporators
- Glycol secondary loop serving the chilled room zones
- Hot gas defrost system for freezer evaporators

Ammonia charge: 1,850 kg (per current plant register)

The system is designed to maintain the freezer hall at –22°C and the chilled storage zones at 2°C. The glycol loop operates as a secondary coolant for the chilled rooms, with the ammonia system providing primary cooling at the plate heat exchanger.

**1. Introduction**

This report records the annual inspection of the ammonia refrigeration system and associated cold-chain monitoring arrangements at Warehouse W-03. The inspection was conducted under the provisions of the Food Act 2003 (NSW) and the NSW Food Safety Authority's Cold Storage Compliance Program.

The scope of the inspection covered:
- Ammonia refrigeration plant and machinery room
- Evaporators and air handling units in the freezer hall and chilled rooms
- Temperature monitoring and calibration systems
- Emergency procedures and safety equipment
- Maintenance records and training documentation

The inspection commenced at 09:15 and concluded at 15:40. The facility was operational throughout, with the freezer hall maintaining a temperature of –22°C ± 1°C and the chilled rooms ranging between 2°C and 4°C.

---

**2. General Observations**

The facility is a purpose-built cold storage warehouse with a total capacity of approximately 14,000 pallet positions. The ammonia refrigeration system consists of two screw compressors (K-101 and K-102), a plate heat exchanger, and a glycol secondary loop serving the chilled rooms. The freezer hall uses direct ammonia expansion.

The plant room was found to be clean and well-ordered. The floor drain traps were primed, and the ventilation system was operating normally. The ammonia detector alarms were tested in the presence of the inspection officer (see Section 4.1).

The site manager, Mr. Hargreaves, was present throughout the inspection and was able to provide access to all areas requested. The previous inspection's non-compliance items (two minor items relating to signage and one observation regarding the spare parts inventory) were reviewed. All three items were found to have been rectified satisfactorily.

---

**3. Refrigeration System – Equipment Condition**

**3.1 Compressors**

| Compressor | Type | Run Hours (at inspection) | Oil Pressure (kPa) | Discharge Pressure (kPa) | Suction Pressure (kPa) | Condition |
|------------|------|---------------------------|--------------------|--------------------------|------------------------|-----------|
| K-101 | Screw | 32,450 | 280 | 1,150 | 310 | Good |
| K-102 | Screw | 24,118 | 275 | 1,140 | 305 | Good |

Both compressors were operating within their design parameters. The oil sight glasses showed clear oil at the correct level. The oil analysis report from 15 May 2024 was sighted; moisture content was reported at 28 ppm, which is below the recommended maximum of 50 ppm.

Compressor K-101 has an oil filter change due in August 2024. This is consistent with the manufacturer's recommended service interval of 12 months. The maintenance plan was updated accordingly during the inspection.

**3.2 Condenser**

The evaporative condenser (model EVAC-200, serial E-1142) was inspected externally. The water distribution troughs were clear of debris, and the drift eliminators were intact. The basin water was tested for conductivity; the reading was 1,850 µS/cm, which is within the recommended range of 1,500–2,500 µS/cm for this installation.

One minor observation: the fan belt on the condenser fan motor showed slight wear (estimated remaining life 3–6 months). This is not a non-compliance item but was recorded as an observation. The site was advised to include this in the next preventive maintenance schedule.

Action: J. Singh to obtain quotes for the sun hood / indicator relocation and report back at the June meeting. Hazard report H-2022-041 to be closed once the mitigation is installed.

---

9. RAIL SIDING – TRANSITION UPDATE

T. Nguyen provided an update on the rail siding project.

- The siding has been operational for transshipment of frozen product since 1 March 2022.
- April throughput: 112 TEU equivalent, below the forecast of 150. The shortfall was due to rolling stock availability, not site constraints.
- Reefer plug points: all 24 points tested and commissioned. Two points were found to have faulty earth leakage protection and were replaced on 28 April.
- The cold-chain risk assessment for the siding is being updated, as noted in item 5. The draft is out for comment and will be finalised by 20 May.

documents.content:
**PORT KEMBLA REGIONAL COLD-CHAIN LOGISTICS COMMITTEE**
**MINUTES OF THE MEETING HELD ON 12 MAY 2022**
**Venue:** Committee Room, Building 4, Port Kembla Terminal
**Time:** 13:30 – 16:05
**Chair:** R. Whitfield
**Attendees:** M. Alvarez, J. Singh, F. Moretti, T. Nguyen, P. Okafor, L. Chen (via video), S. Haddad, D. Kowalski (via video)
**Apologies:** K. Brunton, A. Suleman
**Minutes of previous meeting:** Moved/2nd (Whitfield/Moretti) that the minutes of the 14 April 2022 meeting be accepted as a true record. Carried.

---

**10. QUARTERLY PERFORMANCE REPORT – Q1 2022 (JANUARY–MARCH)**

P. Okafor tabled the Q1 performance report. The report covers all three warehouses (A, B, and C) and the rail siding, which came online partway through the quarter.

- **Throughput:** Total pallet movements were 184,220, up 3.1% on Q4 2021. Warehouse A accounted for 62% of movements, Warehouse B 28%, Warehouse C 10%.
- **Temperature compliance:** 99.2% of logged temperature data points were within the specified range for the product type. The 0.8% variance was concentrated in Warehouse C, mostly during door openings in the 06:00–08:00 shift change.
- **Energy use:** Combined electricity consumption was 2.84 GWh, 4% above forecast. The increase is attributed to a warmer-than-average March and the commissioning of the rail siding reefer points.
- **Labour productivity:** 11.4 pallet movements per labour hour, slightly below the target of 11.8. The shortfall was due to the door incident on 3 May (see item 8) and two days of reduced staffing during the Easter period.

Discussion:
- F. Moretti queried the 0.8% temperature variance. P. Okafor confirmed that no product was condemned or downgraded as a result; all excursions were within the 15-minute corrective action window.
- R. Whitfield asked whether the energy forecast should be revised. L. Chen noted that the forecast had been set before the rail siding was confirmed, and suggested the forecast be updated at the mid-year budget review.
- M. Alvarez noted that the Q1 report shows a recurring pattern of temperature excursions during shift changes over the past six quarters. She asked if this had been analysed. P. Okafor said the data had been reviewed informally but no formal root-cause analysis had been completed. M. Alvarez requested that the matter be added to the risk register for formal investigation.

Action: P. Okafor to prepare a temperature excursion analysis by shift pattern for the June meeting. Action item A-2022-14.

---

**11. INCIDENT FOLLOW-UP – DOOR 6 HAZARD REPORT H-2022-041**

J. Singh reported on the outcome of the hazard report lodged on 13 May, as discussed under item 8.

- Two quotes have been received for the sun hood installation and indicator light relocation. The first quote, from Illawarra Shade & Awnings, is for $3,150 including installation. The second, from Port Fabrication Services, is for $2,780 but with a longer lead time of 6 weeks.
- J. Singh noted that the door manufacturer (Dorstech) has also provided a technical bulletin suggesting that a glare shield could be retrofitted to the existing indicator housing at a cost of $890 for parts only, with installation by our own maintenance team.
- The committee discussed the three options. F. Moretti noted that the Dorstech option is the cheapest but would need to be verified against the glare conditions. M. Alvarez asked whether the maintenance team had capacity to install within 2 weeks. J. Singh confirmed they did.
- R. Whitfield asked whether the glare issue had been formally logged as a hazard prior to the incident. J. Singh confirmed it had not; it had only been raised informally twice in the past year.

Decision: Moved/2nd (Moretti/Alvarez) that the Dorstech glare shield be purchased and installed by the maintenance team, with a follow-up inspection after 4 weeks to confirm effectiveness. If the shield does not resolve the glare, the sun hood option will be revisited. Carried.
